rewrite.noticeThis: Jesus contrasts the thief’s three-part destruction — stealing, slaughtering, and destroying — with a single, overflowing purpose: that his sheep may have life in abundance.

insight_issue: The insight commits Trench's lexical fallacy by claiming zōē inherently denotes a distinct non-biological 'kind' of life over against bios and psychē; bios never occurs in John, and psychē is precisely what the Good Shepherd lays down for the sheep in verse 11.

rewrite.noticeThis: The doubled 'peace, peace' is Hebrew’s way of expressing complete, unbroken wholeness, promised to a mind (yetzer) that is sāmuḵ — steadily resting its full weight on God.
rewrite.whyItMatters: This peace is not circumstantial calm, but the steady reality of a mind that stops trying to hold itself up and leans its full weight onto God in trust.
rewrite.carryItWithYou: Notice one anxious thought pattern today, and instead of trying to think your way out of it, consciously lean its weight onto God in a spoken act of trust.
